title: Opening Night at Salt
teaser: At the opening of the restaurant Salt, critic Irina Valevskaya tried the third course of the tasting menu and told the chef in front of the guests: "After the fourth, I'll write about what was in the third." She never got the fourth. She was found dead in the wine cellar, where she'd gone down "to have a look at the collection". The restaurant doors were shut until the police arrive.

habits.label: Burns on the arms
habits.habit: Forearms covered in small burns from pans
clues: The glass door of the wine cellar has a forearm print, and the skin on it is blotchy, as if from burns. The culprit has burns on their arms.
An open tube of burn cream without its cap lies in the hot kitchen's first-aid kit. The culprit has burns on their arms.

habits.label: Smells of garlic
clues: The wine cellar smells of cork and cold, but the handle of a rack reeks of garlic. The culprit smells of garlic.
The service corridor door has a palm print with a sharp smell of garlic. The culprit smells of garlic.

habits.label: Icing sugar
clues: A dark bottle in the wine cellar has a white film of icing sugar on it, as if picked up by a hand fresh from the pastry kitchen. The culprit has icing sugar on their sleeves.
There's a white stripe of icing sugar on the black tablecloth at the chef's table, like from a sleeve. The culprit has icing sugar on their sleeves.

habits.label: Blue plaster
habits.habit: A finger wrapped in a blue kitchen plaster
clues: A blue plaster lies on the wine cellar floor. Kitchens use them so they're easy to spot if one falls into the food. The culprit has a finger wrapped in a blue plaster.
A scrap of blue plaster is floating in a glass at the bar. The culprit has a finger wrapped in a blue plaster.

habits.label: White clogs
clues: The stairs to the wine cellar show the print of a wide rubber sole, like kitchen clogs. The culprit wears white clogs.
A puddle on the summer terrace has the print of a clog's round toe. The culprit wears white clogs.

habits.label: Towel on the shoulder
habits.habit: Always has a towel slung over their shoulder
clues: Valevskaya was strangled in the cellar with something soft: her neck shows marks of thick terry cloth. The culprit keeps a towel on their shoulder.
A towel with brown stains hangs on a hook in the service corridor, and nobody will admit it's theirs. The culprit keeps a towel on their shoulder.

habits.label: Toothpick
clues: A chewed toothpick, still damp, lies between the bottles in the wine cellar. The culprit chews a toothpick.
Two chewed-up toothpicks lie in an ashtray on the summer terrace. The culprit chews a toothpick.

habits.label: Wine stain
habits.habit: A red wine stain on their cuff
clues: A rack in the wine cellar has a red mark from a cuff, though not a single bottle is broken. The culprit has red wine on their cuff.
A white towel at the bar has a red stain, as if someone tried to rub a cuff clean with it. The culprit has red wine on their cuff.

habits.label: Carnation buttonhole
habits.habit: A fresh carnation in the buttonhole
clues: A red carnation petal lies under Valevskaya's hand, and the dining room has only white flowers. The culprit wears a carnation in their buttonhole.
A crushed carnation with a pin lies on a table on the summer terrace. The culprit wears a carnation in their buttonhole.

habits.label: Signet ring
habits.habit: A gold signet on the little finger
clues: Valevskaya has a small square bruise with a monogram on her cheek, like from a blow by a hand wearing a signet ring. The culprit wears a signet ring.
The stem of a glass at the bar is scratched, as if held by a hand with a heavy ring. The culprit wears a signet ring.

habits.label: Grey streak
habits.habit: A grey streak in dark hair
clues: Valevskaya is clutching a grey hair, and she's a redhead. The culprit has a grey streak.
A chef's jacket in the service corridor has a grey hair among dark ones on its collar. The culprit has a grey streak.

habits.label: Smells of vanilla
clues: The sommelier says that when he found the body, the cellar smelled of vanilla, though nothing sweet is kept there. The culprit smells of vanilla.
The back of a chair on the summer terrace still smells of vanilla. The culprit smells of vanilla.

habits.label: Gelled hair
clues: A collector's bottle in the cellar has a shiny greasy mark, like from a palm used to smooth down gelled hair. The culprit wears hair gel.
An open tub of hair gel stands in the staff toilet next to the service corridor. The culprit wears hair gel.

habits.label: Knife tattoo
habits.habit: A chef's knife tattooed on the forearm
clues: The waitress saw an arm with a knife tattoo on the forearm in the wine cellar doorway. The culprit has a knife tattoo.
At 22:05 the food photographer was shooting the hot kitchen, and an arm with a tattooed knife got into the frame. The culprit has a knife tattoo.

habits.label: Timer round the neck
habits.habit: A kitchen timer hangs round their neck
clues: The bartender heard a kitchen timer beep for a second in the wine cellar. The culprit wears a timer round their neck.
A torn cord with a clip from a kitchen timer lies on the stairs to the wine cellar. The culprit wears a timer round their neck.

habits.label: Glasses on a chain
clues: A bead from a glasses chain lies under a rack in the wine cellar. The culprit wears glasses on a chain.
Guests at the chef's table remember someone going out into the service corridor, holding their glasses on a chain. The culprit wears glasses on a chain.

tools: The wine cellar lock was opened not with a key but with an oyster knife, without damaging the latch. The culprit is handy with tools.
The cooling hose in the cellar was neatly pinched with a clamp so the sensor wouldn't beep. The culprit is handy with tools.
sched: The menu has exactly twelve minutes between the third and fourth courses, and someone was waiting for Valevskaya in the cellar during that gap. The culprit knows the schedule.
The sommelier goes down to the cellar every half hour, and it all happened right after his last visit. The culprit knows the schedule.
strong: Valevskaya was lifted and sat on a barrel by the far rack, as if she had nodded off. The culprit is physically strong.
A rack of bottles weighing nearly two hundred kilos was moved to block the passage. The culprit is physically strong.
french: On Valevskaya's menu, under the name Salt, someone has written "Le dernier plat", French for "The last course". The culprit knows French.
A bottle of Burgundy in the cellar has "Pour elle", meaning "For her", written on it in chalk. The culprit knows French.
quiet: Every third step on the cellar stairs creaks, but nobody in the dining room heard anyone go down. The culprit moves silently.
The bartender sat by the door to the service corridor and swears nobody went past. The culprit moves silently.
keys: The collection cellar is locked, and only the sommelier and the owner had keys, yet the door was opened without force. The culprit had keys.
The cold room in the hot kitchen is locked, yet a tin of caviar is missing from it. The culprit had keys.
cash: By the end of the evening the bar till is short by exactly the price of one tasting menu. The culprit had access to money.
Valevskaya's bill was closed as paid, though she paid nothing. The culprit had access to money.
safe: The safe in the owner's office, where the supplier contracts were kept, is open, and one contract is missing. The culprit knows the safe combination.
The combination cabinet with expensive bottles in the cellar is open, and one bottle is missing. The culprit knows the safe combination.
passages: A bottle lift runs from the hot kitchen to the wine cellar. Only the cooks use it, and right now it's at the bottom. The culprit knows the service passages.
A door for taking out the rubbish leads from the summer terrace to the service corridor, and someone has bolted it from inside. The culprit knows the service passages.
tech: The camera in the wine cellar stopped recording at 22:02: it was switched off through the app. The culprit knows their way around machinery.
The temperature sensor in the cellar was turned off so the alarm wouldn't go off when the door opened. The culprit knows their way around machinery.
driver: The fish supplier's van has been moved from the service entrance to the terrace, and its engine is still warm. The culprit can drive.
Valevskaya's car was moved into the next lane, though she'd handed her keys to the cloakroom attendant. The culprit can drive.
medic: The mushroom sauce in the third course Valevskaya ate contained death cap, in a dose meant to stun, not kill. The culprit knows about poisons.
Valevskaya's glass at the chef's table had traces of a heart drug dissolved in the red wine. The culprit knows about poisons.
